pattern.description: A vi editor window composited beside the talking-head presenter scrolls its code listing upward in discrete line jumps inside the fixed rounded window mask while the presenter talks about large files.
pattern.why_premium: Real code scrolling inside a clean, gradient-backed window gives live-product proof without cutting away from the presenter; the window frame stays perfectly still so only the content moves.

build_hint.gsap: Keep the editor window static with overflow hidden; animate the inner code container's y in 3 quick steps: gsap.timeline().to(code, {y: '-=Nline', duration: 0.05, ease: 'none'}).to(code, {y: '-=Nline', duration: 0.05, ease: 'none'}, '+=0.06')... (or ease: 'steps(1)'), gutter numbers bound to the same y.
build_hint.remotion: Inside an overflow:hidden window, translateY of the code block = -lineHeight * Math.floor(interpolate(frame, [0, 20], [0, totalLines], {extrapolateRight: 'clamp'})) to reproduce stepped editor scrolling; no spring.

notes: Energy curve shows three distinct short bursts, consistent with stepped editor scrolling (key-repeat or page jumps) rather than a smooth eased scroll. b03/b05/b04 are parts of one scrolling code block. Camera move is none; the pan/scale sums reflect the in-window scroll only.
